note: Adjudicated differences between the design hand-off's prop surface and this kit's. `kind: renamed | boolean-axis | web-only | intentional-omission` means the capability EXISTS in Canvas under another spelling, or is deliberately not offered — these are settled and need no action. `kind: open-gap` means the capability is genuinely missing and is acknowledged; `plannedIn` names the phase that closes it, or `unscheduled`. scripts/check-handoff-parity.ts fails on any difference recorded in NEITHER place, so a hand-off revision surfaces loudly.

onClick.reason: React Native has no onClick; press handling is onPress across the whole kit.

type.reason: The DOM <input type> attribute. Canvas carries the shape rule as `validateAs` and the masking as `password`/`masked`.

glass.reason: Glass is a theming-level surface mode in Canvas (`<ThemeProvider glass>` / `data-surface`), never a per-component prop. CLAUDE.md forbids adding one.

onClose.reason: Canvas's controllable-state convention pairs `open`/`defaultOpen` with `onOpenChange`, which reports both directions rather than close only.

size.reason: Canvas rejects string and numeric size props; every size axis is flat booleans (CLAUDE.md 'Semantic prop styling').

align.reason: String-enum alignment is rejected; Canvas spells the non-default end as a boolean.

side.reason: String-enum placement is rejected; Canvas spells each side as its own boolean.

onChange.reason: Canvas names the callback for what it reports, per the controllable-state naming table.

value.reason: Canvas names the controlled prop for the concept it holds (`selected`, `active`) rather than a generic `value`.

defaultValue.reason: Paired seed prop for the renamed controlled prop above.

height.reason: Canvas charts size themselves from the skin's plot height and the `compact` axis, so a caller never hand-sets a pixel height.

xLabels.reason: The cartesian frame calls its category axis `labels`; there is no second label axis to disambiguate from.

yTicks.reason: Canvas's chart-math nices the domain and picks its own tick count; `min`/`max` bound it instead.

helper.reason: The muted hint line under a field. Only Autocomplete has one today (as `helperText`, unlinked for a11y); Field and the shared message chrome give every field family one.

bare.reason: Drop the chart's card surface so it can embed in an existing one. Canvas charts always paint their own card; ChartFrame gains `bare` in phase 5 but the nine series charts do not.

subtitle.reason: A muted second line under a chart title. Canvas charts carry `title` only.

unit.reason: A unit suffix on chart values. Canvas expects `formatValue` to append it, which cannot reach every readout.

crosshair.reason: A tracking crosshair on hover/scrub. Canvas ships scrub-to-inspect with a value flag instead, which is a different affordance.

defaultOpen.reason: Canvas's accordion is value-driven (`value`/`defaultValue`/`onValueChange`) so single and multiple modes share one API.

action.reason: Canvas splits the action into its label and its handler rather than taking a ReactNode, so the panel owns the button's look.

children.reason: The panel's body text is the `description` prop, per the 'components own their label anatomy' rule.

stacked.reason: Canvas names the opposite end of the same axis; omitting `inline` gives the stacked layout.

items.reason: Named `actions` to match the sheet's other action-bearing props.

confirmField.reason: Canvas splits type-to-confirm into the boolean that turns it on and the string that must be matched.

dismissible.reason: An alert dialog is modal by contract in Canvas: it must be resolved through confirm or cancel, so scrim-dismiss is not offered.

width.reason: Pixel widths are rejected; the width axis is flat booleans.

helper.reason: Already present under this name; phase 3 aligns the a11y wiring, not the spelling.

separator.reason: String-enum separator is rejected; each glyph is its own boolean.

value.reason: The group's controlled prop is `active`, paired with `defaultActive`/`onSelect`.

onChange.reason: Reports the selected item, so it is named for what it reports.

start.reason: Canvas takes the displayed month and the week's first day rather than one opaque start date.

days.reason: Named for what it counts, since `day` is a separate single-day prop.

ma.reason: Canvas takes a general overlay series list, of which a moving average is one case.

priceAxis.reason: Canvas always renders the price axis; `hideAxes` is the only control.

lastPrice.reason: A dashed last-price rule with a label tab. Canvas has no equivalent marker.

currency.reason: Canvas formats values through one callback rather than a currency code plus a precision.

decimals.reason: Precision is the caller's formatter, not a separate knob.

children.reason: Canvas's candlestick owns its plot; extra marks go through `overlays` rather than arbitrary children.

slides.reason: Every collection component in Canvas takes `items`.

swipe.reason: Swipe is always on in Canvas; on native it is the primary gesture and disabling it would strand touch users.

tone.reason: The one place the hand-off uses a union for the intent axis; Canvas spells it as booleans like everywhere else.

label.reason: Canvas names the disclosure's heading `title`, matching Card and Popover.

onReorder.reason: Canvas's controllable-state convention pairs `order`/`defaultOrder` with `onOrderChange`, the same pairing `onClose` to `onOpenChange` records above.

locked.reason: Renamed and deliberately inverted. A dashboard is static in normal use and reorderable only in an explicit customize mode, so the absent default has to be the static one; a `locked` prop would make every consumer pass it just to get ordinary behavior. Locked is also the cheaper state here, mounting no drag provider at all.

gap.reason: Raw numeric spacing is rejected; gutters come from the named spacing scale, and the grid exposes the one it varies as the density axis.

columns.reason: The board is twelve columns by definition, and a widget states its width as a span within them. A caller-set track count would leave `span` meaning nothing, since the same 6 would be half a board or the whole of it.

rowHeight.reason: Rows are sized by their content, because a widget arrives with its own surface and owns its height (a Card, a Chart, a Stats row). A fixed row height would clip the tall ones and stretch the short ones.

footer.reason: A summary/footer row under the body. Canvas has no footer slot.

sortDir.reason: Canvas carries column and direction together in one `sort` object so they cannot drift apart.

onSort.reason: Controllable-state naming: the change callback for the `sort` prop.

onEdit.reason: Prefixed to say what is edited, since the table also commits cells.

onSave.reason: Canvas distinguishes committing a whole row from committing one cell during inline edit.

rowActions.reason: Canvas drives the per-row affordances from the edit/delete handlers plus `inlineEdit` rather than an action descriptor list.

emptyLabel.reason: Named `message` because it is a sentence, not a label.

mid.reason: The mid-price marker between bid and ask walls. Canvas derives the split but draws no marker.

depthAxis.reason: Canvas always renders the depth axis; `hideAxes` is the only control.

currency.reason: One formatter callback rather than a currency code.

decimals.reason: Precision belongs to the caller's formatter.

layout.reason: String-enum layout is rejected; each arrangement is its own boolean.

bordered.reason: Canvas names it for the hairlines between rows, not a box around them.

width.reason: Pixel widths are rejected; the size axis is already flat booleans here.

label.reason: The divider owns its label as children, per 'components own their label anatomy'.

title.reason: Canvas's Drawer is a bare panel; the caller supplies its own header. The hand-off's owns title/description/footer chrome.

size.reason: Canvas sizes a side drawer with a pixel `width` (default 288), not a size axis; it is ignored for the bottom/top sheet, which spans the edge it rises from.

action.reason: Label plus handler rather than a ReactNode, so the empty state owns its button's look.

avatars.reason: One boolean turning the avatar column on, rather than a list; each item carries its own image.

max.reason: Canvas's Gauge is fixed to a 0-100 percentage, which is what its semicircle readout is built around.

size.reason: A size axis for the dial. GaugeProps carries no size lever at all, so a Gauge is one size everywhere. This was recorded as a settled boolean axis pointing at `small`/`large`, which the component has never had.

columns.reason: A numeric column count is rejected; the two supported densities are booleans that also drive the responsive collapse.

renderItem.reason: Canvas's GridList owns its tile anatomy from `items`; a render prop would let callers rebuild the tile and drift from the kit.

days.reason: Canvas takes one flat value series and derives the calendar grid from it.

startDay.reason: Which weekday the grid starts on. Canvas fixes it.

rows.reason: Canvas derives the grid shape from the data and the `calendar` mode rather than taking explicit dimensions.

color.reason: The ramp comes from the chart tokens so every heatmap in a product reads alike.

title.reason: Canvas's Heatmap names its heading `label`, paired with `caption`.

cell.reason: Cell size is a skin metric, not a caller knob.

gap.reason: Gutter is a skin metric; a raw gap would be a styling escape hatch.

legend.reason: Canvas shows the legend by default and takes the inverse boolean to suppress it.

name.reason: Canvas exposes every glyph as its own boolean prop (`<Icon shield />`), so the glyph set is type-checked at the call site rather than stringly-typed.

iconLeft.reason: Canvas pairs one `icon` glyph with the boolean that places it.

password.reason: Masking plus a reveal toggle the field owns. Canvas has `masked` on InputOTP only, so every caller currently wires its own eye button.

onBlur.reason: Needed by the validation display gate, which reports on blur.

minLength.reason: Part of the validation rule chain.

maxLength.reason: Part of the validation rule chain (a reporting rule, not a hard cap).

pattern.reason: Part of the validation rule chain.

min.reason: Part of the validation rule chain.

max.reason: Part of the validation rule chain.

validateOn.reason: Chooses when rules start reporting (blur, then live).

submitted.reason: Forces every field to report for a form's submit pass.

showValid.reason: The success border and tick once a value passes.

onValidate.reason: Reports the current error to the parent.

active.reason: The focused cell is internal state; exposing it would let a caller desync the caret from the value.

numeric.reason: Canvas names the INVERSE boolean. The hand-off's `numeric` defaults to true, and a default-true boolean reads backwards against the semantic-prop rule that passing a prop turns it on, so the kit spells the opt-out (`alphanumeric` accepts letters and asks for the text keyboard) the way `hideLegend`/`hideGrid`/`hideAxes` do.

smooth.reason: Canvas names the curve interpolation `curved` across every cartesian chart.

area.reason: Filling under the line is a separate component in Canvas rather than a mode of LineChart.

yAxis.reason: Canvas bounds the axis with two scalars rather than a domain tuple.

valueLabels.reason: Printing each datum's value beside its point. Canvas shows values only on scrub.

options.reason: Every collection component in Canvas takes `items`.

value.reason: Named for the concept it holds, paired with `defaultSelected`/`onSelect`.

multiple.reason: Canvas's spelling of the same boolean.

media.reason: Canvas takes the leading visual as a typed slot per kind rather than one opaque node.

align.reason: String-enum alignment is rejected; each is its own boolean.

title.reason: Canvas names the leading identity slot `brand`, which also carries the mark.

items.reason: Named for what they are, since the bar also carries actions and an avatar.

actions.reason: Label plus handler rather than a ReactNode, so the bar owns the button's look.

pages.reason: Canvas derives the page count from the item total and page size so the two cannot disagree.

data.reason: Named for what a pie is made of, matching `series` on the cartesian charts.

thickness.reason: Canvas offers the donut as a boolean with a token-set ring width rather than a caller pixel value.

centerLabel.reason: Text in the donut hole. Canvas leaves the hole empty.

sliceLabels.reason: Labels drawn on the slices themselves; Canvas labels only in the legend.

legend.reason: Shown by default; the inverse boolean suppresses it.

size.reason: Canvas spells the size change as its density axis: `compact` takes the chart from 160 to 120 and the centre readout from 24 to 20. There is one smaller step and no larger one, so the hand-off's `large` has no equivalent.

width.reason: The popover sizes to its content and the skin's max width; a pixel width would be a styling escape hatch.

label.reason: Progress owns its label as children, with `description` for the second line.

index.reason: Canvas staggers from document order rather than a caller-supplied index.

from.reason: String-enum direction is rejected; each is its own boolean.

deep.reason: Canvas names the threshold boolean for what it means: wait until the element is well inside the viewport.

xTitle.reason: An axis title under the x axis. Canvas labels ticks but titles no axis.

yTitle.reason: As above, rotated beside the y axis.

trend.reason: A fitted trend line through the points.

xTicks.reason: Canvas's chart-math nices both domains and picks its own tick counts.

grid.reason: Shown by default; the inverse boolean suppresses it.

circle.reason: Canvas names its shapes for what they stand in for (`avatar`, `text`, `card`, `table`, `list`, `button`) rather than for their geometry.

width.reason: Shape presets carry their own dimensions; a raw width would be a styling escape hatch.

label.reason: Slider owns its title as children, with `description` for the second line.

data.reason: Canvas names the plain number series `values`.

width.reason: The strip fills its container; a pixel width would be a styling escape hatch.

height.reason: Two heights are offered as a boolean rather than a pixel value.

color.reason: A raw color is a styling escape hatch; the tone axis is booleans onto the tokens.

label.reason: Spinner owns its label as children, with `description` for the second line.

style.reason: Spinner takes no style prop; it is sized by its boolean axis and positioned by its parent.

categories.reason: Canvas's StackedBar is a single proportional strip whose parts each carry their own label, so there is no category axis to name. The cartesian `labels` prop belongs to the multi-column charts and does not exist here.

series.reason: Canvas's StackedBar is a single proportional bar whose parts are `segments`, not a multi-series cartesian chart.

title.reason: Canvas's StackedBar is a bare strip meant to sit inside a Card that carries the heading.

grouped.reason: Side-by-side grouping is Chart's job in Canvas; StackedBar always stacks.

stretch.reason: The strip always fills its container width.

yAxis.reason: A proportional strip has no value axis.

totals.reason: Printing each stack's total above the bar.

compact.reason: The strip has one density; its height is a skin metric.

headerAction.reason: An action in the list's header row. Canvas's StackedList has no header slot.

divided.reason: Canvas always draws the row hairlines; they are what makes it a stacked list.

onItemClick.reason: React Native press naming, with the object the handler reports last: `onPressItem`.

selectedId.reason: Marking one row as current. Canvas's StackedList is not selectable.

columns.reason: Stats reflows intrinsically from a minimum tile width rather than a fixed column count, so it adapts inside any parent.

searchKey.reason: Marking one tab as the search tab, which iOS treats specially.

accessory.reason: A slot above the bar for a now-playing style accessory.

minimized.reason: The controlled counterpart of the above.

scrollRef.reason: The scroll view the bar watches to drive minimizing.

items.reason: Named for what they are, matching the component.

maxLength.reason: Part of the validation rule chain; Textarea already uses maxLength for `showCount` but not as a reporting rule.

title.reason: Toast owns its text as `message`, with `description` for the second line.

onClose.reason: Canvas's Toast reports dismissal only (there is no open/close duality to report), so the callback is named for what it reports.

children.reason: Wrapping an arbitrary node as the tooltip target. Canvas's Tooltip renders its own trigger from a `trigger` string in one of three flavors (button, icon button, inline word) and cannot attach to a caller's node.

reveal.reason: Choosing the entrance animation (lift, scale, fade, none). Canvas fixes one reveal.

brisk.reason: Running the reveal at 90ms instead of 140ms. Canvas fixes the timing on Tooltip (its Reveal component does expose `brisk`).

as.reason: Choosing the rendered HTML element. React Native has no element to choose; the role props set the type scale and the accessibility role.

ChartFrame.reason: The public chart wrapper (card surface, title, axis gutter, legend) taking a plain children plot. Canvas has the internal render-prop CartesianFrame and the internal chartShell, but exposes neither.

avatar-size-scale.reason: The whole scale sits one step high. The prop check cannot see this: `small` and `large` exist on both sides, so it reports them satisfied while the diameters differ. Re-scaling shipped avatars is a visual break for every consumer, so it is tracked rather than done; the `tiny` 24 step was added for the AvatarMenu pill inset without moving the rest.
